name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Ruby ${{ matrix.ruby }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        ruby:
          - '3.1'
          - '3.2'
          - '3.3'
          - '3.4'
          - '4.0'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@d45b1a4e94b71acab930e56e79c6aa188764e7f9 # v1.316.0
        with:
          ruby-version: ${{ matrix.ruby }}
          bundler-cache: true
      - run: bundle exec rake test

  quality:
    name: Lint and build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@d45b1a4e94b71acab930e56e79c6aa188764e7f9 # v1.316.0
        with:
          ruby-version: '4.0'
          bundler-cache: true
      - run: bundle exec rubocop
      - run: bundle exec rake yard
      - run: bundle exec rake rdoc
      - run: gem build ruby_llm-voyage.gemspec

  lint-actions:
    name: GitHub Actions audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run actionlint
        uses: rhysd/actionlint@914e7df21a07ef503a81201c76d2b11c789d3fca # v1.7.12

      - name: Run zizmor
        uses: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@192e21d79ab29983730a13d1382995c2307fbcaa # v0.5.7
        with:
          advanced-security: false

Gem::Specification.new do |spec|
  spec.name = 'ruby_llm-voyage'
  spec.version = RubyLLM::Voyage::VERSION
  spec.authors = ['Daniel Insley']
  spec.email = ['dan@insley.ca']
  spec.summary = 'Voyage retrieval APIs for RubyLLM'
  spec.description = 'A RubyLLM extension for Voyage embeddings, reranking, contextualized chunks, and files.'
  spec.homepage = 'https://github.com/dinsley/ruby_llm-voyage'
  spec.license = 'MIT'
  spec.required_ruby_version = '>= 3.1.3'

  spec.metadata['homepage_uri'] = spec.homepage
  spec.metadata['source_code_uri'] = "#{spec.homepage}/tree/v#{spec.version}"
  spec.metadata['changelog_uri'] = "#{spec.homepage}/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
  spec.metadata['bug_tracker_uri'] = "#{spec.homepage}/issues"
  spec.metadata['documentation_uri'] = "https://www.rubydoc.info/gems/#{spec.name}/#{spec.version}"
  spec.metadata['allowed_push_host'] = 'https://rubygems.org'
  spec.metadata['rubygems_mfa_required'] = 'true'

  spec.files = Dir[
    'lib/**/*',
    'docs/**/*',
    'CHANGELOG.md',
    'CONTRIBUTING.md',
    'LICENSE.txt',
    'README.md',
    'SECURITY.md'
  ]
  spec.extra_rdoc_files = %w[README.md CHANGELOG.md LICENSE.txt]
  spec.rdoc_options = ['--main', 'README.md', '--markup', 'markdown']
  spec.require_paths = ['lib']

  spec.add_dependency 'ruby_llm', '>= 1.16', '< 2.0'
end

name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions: {}

jobs:
  release:
    name: Publish to RubyGems
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # No dependency cache: a poisoned cache could reach the published gem.
      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@d45b1a4e94b71acab930e56e79c6aa188764e7f9 # v1.316.0
        with:
          ruby-version: '4.0'
      - run: bundle install
      - run: bundle exec rake test
      - uses: rubygems/release-gem@052cc82692552de3ef2b81fd670e41d13cba8092 # v1.4.0

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'ruby_llm'
require 'ruby_llm/voyage'

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'ruby_llm'
require 'ruby_llm/voyage/version'
require 'ruby_llm/voyage/results'
require 'ruby_llm/voyage/vector_decoder'
require 'ruby_llm/providers/voyage'

# RubyLLM framework namespace.
module RubyLLM
  # Voyage retrieval APIs for RubyLLM: embeddings, reranking, contextualized
  # chunk embeddings, and files.
  module Voyage
    # Generates embeddings with a Voyage text embedding model.
    #
    # This facade exposes Voyage-specific options that are not first-class
    # keywords on +RubyLLM.embed+ in RubyLLM 1.x. It returns the same
    # {RubyLLM::Embedding} result type and emits the same instrumentation event.
    #
    # @param text [String, Array<String>] one input or a batch of inputs
    # @param model [String, nil] Voyage model ID, such as +voyage-4-lite+;
    #   defaults to +config.default_embedding_model+
    # @param dimensions [Integer, nil] requested output dimensions; defaults
    #   to +config.voyage_default_output_dimension+
    # @param input_type [String, Symbol, nil] +query+, +document+, or +nil+
    # @param truncation [Boolean, nil] whether Voyage may truncate long inputs
    # @param output_dtype [String, Symbol, nil] +float+, +int8+, +uint8+,
    #   +binary+, +ubinary+, or +nil+
    # @param encoding_format [String, Symbol, nil] +base64+ or +nil+
    # @param provider_options [Hash] trusted fields merged into the Voyage
    #   request after named options
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil] isolated RubyLLM configuration
    # @return [RubyLLM::Embedding] vectors, model ID, and input-token usage
    # @raise [RubyLLM::ConfigurationError] when the Voyage API key is missing
    # @raise [RubyLLM::Error] when Voyage returns an unsuccessful response
    #
    # @example Embed a retrieval query
    #   embedding = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed(
    #     "How do I configure SSO?",
    #     model: "voyage-4-lite",
    #     input_type: :query,
    #     dimensions: 512
    #   )
    #   embedding.vectors #=> Array<Float>
    def self.embed(text, model: nil, dimensions: nil, input_type: UNSET, truncation: UNSET, output_dtype: UNSET,
                   encoding_format: UNSET, provider_options: {}, context: nil)
      validate_input!(:text, text)
      config = context&.config || RubyLLM.config
      model ||= config.default_embedding_model
      provider = Providers::Voyage.new(config)
      payload = {
        provider: provider.slug,
        model: model,
        input: text,
        dimensions: dimensions,
        input_type: input_type,
        truncation: truncation,
        output_dtype: output_dtype,
        encoding_format: encoding_format
      }.reject { |_key, value| value.equal?(UNSET) }

      RubyLLM.instrument('embedding.ruby_llm', payload, config:) do |event|
        result = provider.embed(
          text,
          model:,
          dimensions:,
          input_type:,
          truncation:,
          output_dtype:,
          encoding_format:,
          provider_options:
        )
        event[:result] = result
        event[:response_model] = result.model
        event[:input_tokens] = result.input_tokens
        result
      end
    end

    # Embeds search text for the query side of retrieval.
    #
    # Equivalent to {.embed} with +input_type: 'query'+. Pair with
    # {.embed_documents} so Voyage optimizes both sides of retrieval, and
    # configure +default_embedding_model+ and +voyage_default_output_dimension+ once
    # to keep call sites small.
    #
    # @param text [String, Array<String>] one search input or a batch
    # @param options [Hash] the same options as {.embed}, except +input_type+
    # @return [RubyLLM::Embedding]
    # @raise [ArgumentError] when +input_type+ is passed
    #
    # @example
    #   RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_query('How do I configure SSO?').vectors
    def self.embed_query(text, **options)
      embed_side(text, 'query', __method__, options)
    end

    # Embeds content for the document side of retrieval.
    #
    # Equivalent to {.embed} with +input_type: 'document'+. Accepts one text
    # or a batch of up to 1,000.
    #
    # @param texts [String, Array<String>] content to index
    # @param options [Hash] the same options as {.embed}, except +input_type+
    # @return [RubyLLM::Embedding]
    # @raise [ArgumentError] when +input_type+ is passed
    #
    # @example
    #   RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_documents(articles.map(&:content)).vectors
    def self.embed_documents(texts, **options)
      embed_side(texts, 'document', __method__, options)
    end

    # Reranks documents for a query with a Voyage reranker.
    # @param query [String]
    # @param documents [Array<String>]
    # @param model [String]
    # @param top_k [Integer, nil]
    # @param return_documents [Boolean]
    # @param truncation [Boolean]
    # @param provider_options [Hash]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::Reranking]
    def self.rerank(query:, documents:, model: 'rerank-2.5-lite', top_k: nil, return_documents: UNSET,
                    truncation: UNSET, provider_options: {}, context: nil)
      validate_input!(:query, query)
      validate_input!(:documents, documents)
      config = context&.config || RubyLLM.config
      provider = Providers::Voyage.new(config)
      payload = { model: model, query: query, document_count: documents.length }
      RubyLLM.instrument('rerank.voyage', payload, config:) do |event|
        result = provider.rerank(
          query:, documents:, model:, top_k:, return_documents:, truncation:, provider_options:
        )
        event[:result] = result
        event[:response_model] = result.model
        event[:input_tokens] = result.input_tokens
        result
      end
    end

    # Generates context-aware embeddings for grouped document chunks.
    # @param inputs [Array<String>, Array<Array<String>>]
    # @param model [String]
    # @param input_type [String, Symbol, nil]
    # @param dimensions [Integer, nil] defaults to
    #   +config.voyage_default_output_dimension+
    # @param output_dtype [String, Symbol, nil]
    # @param encoding_format [String, Symbol, nil]
    # @param auto_chunk [Boolean, nil]
    # @param chunk_size [Integer, nil]
    # @param chunk_overlap [Integer, nil]
    # @param provider_options [Hash]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedEmbedding]
    def self.contextualized_embed(inputs, model: 'voyage-context-4', input_type: UNSET, dimensions: nil,
                                  output_dtype: UNSET, encoding_format: UNSET, auto_chunk: nil, chunk_size: nil,
                                  chunk_overlap: nil, provider_options: {}, context: nil)
      validate_input!(:inputs, inputs)
      config = context&.config || RubyLLM.config
      provider = Providers::Voyage.new(config)
      payload = { model: model, input_count: inputs.length, input_type: input_type, auto_chunk: auto_chunk }
                .reject { |_key, value| value.equal?(UNSET) }
      RubyLLM.instrument('contextualized_embedding.voyage', payload, config:) do |event|
        result = provider.contextualized_embed(
          inputs, model:, input_type:, dimensions:, output_dtype:, encoding_format:, auto_chunk:, chunk_size:,
                  chunk_overlap:, provider_options:
        )
        event[:result] = result
        event[:response_model] = result.model
        event[:input_tokens] = result.input_tokens
        result
      end
    end

    # Uploads a JSONL file to Voyage.
    # @param path [String, Pathname]
    # @param purpose [String]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::VoyageFile]
    def self.upload_file(path, purpose: 'batch', context: nil)
      provider_for(context).upload_file(path, purpose:)
    end

    # Retrieves metadata for one Voyage file.
    # @param file_id [String]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::VoyageFile]
    def self.retrieve_file(file_id, context: nil)
      provider_for(context).retrieve_file(file_id)
    end

    # Lists Voyage files with cursor pagination.
    # @param purpose [String, nil]
    # @param limit [Integer, nil]
    # @param order [String, Symbol, nil]
    # @param after [String, nil]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::Page]
    def self.list_files(purpose: nil, limit: nil, order: nil, after: nil, context: nil)
      provider_for(context).list_files(purpose:, limit:, order: order&.to_s, after:)
    end

    # Downloads a Voyage file's raw contents.
    # @param file_id [String]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [String]
    def self.file_content(file_id, context: nil)
      provider_for(context).file_content(file_id)
    end

    # Deletes one or more Voyage files atomically.
    # @param file_ids [Array<String>]
    # @param context [RubyLLM::Context, nil]
    # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::FileDeletion]
    def self.delete_files(file_ids, context: nil)
      provider_for(context).delete_files(file_ids)
    end

    class << self
      # Alias of {.retrieve_file}, matching the +find_file+ naming used by
      # RubyLLM's provider file API.
      alias find_file retrieve_file

      # Alias of {.file_content}, matching the +download_file+ naming used by
      # RubyLLM's provider file API.
      alias download_file file_content
    end

    # Builds a configured Voyage provider for resource operations.
    # @api private
    def self.provider_for(context)
      Providers::Voyage.new(context&.config || RubyLLM.config)
    end
    private_class_method :provider_for

    # Fails fast on inputs Voyage would reject, before any network request.
    # @api private
    def self.validate_input!(name, value)
      raise ArgumentError, "#{name} cannot be nil" if value.nil?
      raise ArgumentError, "#{name} cannot be empty" if value.respond_to?(:empty?) && value.empty?
    end
    private_class_method :validate_input!

    # Embeds one retrieval side with a fixed input type.
    # @api private
    def self.embed_side(text, input_type, method_name, options)
      if options.key?(:input_type)
        raise ArgumentError, "#{method_name} sets input_type: '#{input_type}'; use embed to pass another input_type"
      end

      embed(text, input_type: input_type, **options)
    end
    private_class_method :embed_side
  end
end

RubyLLM::Provider.register :voyage, RubyLLM::Providers::Voyage

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RubyLLM
  module Voyage
    # Decodes Voyage Base64 vector representations.
    #
    # The gem decodes API responses automatically; use this directly when
    # parsing embeddings out of Voyage batch result files, which contain the
    # same Base64 encoding.
    module VectorDecoder
      module_function

      # Decodes a Base64 vector for the requested Voyage output type.
      # @param vector [String] Base64-encoded vector data
      # @param output_dtype [String, Symbol, nil] the +output_dtype+ the
      #   embedding was requested with; +nil+ decodes as +float+
      # @return [Array<Float>, Array<Integer>]
      # @raise [ArgumentError] when the Base64 data or output type is invalid
      #
      # @example Decode an embedding from a batch results file
      #   line = JSON.parse(jsonl_line)
      #   encoded = line.dig('response', 'body', 'data', 0, 'embedding')
      #   RubyLLM::Voyage::VectorDecoder.decode(encoded, :float)
      def decode(vector, output_dtype)
        # unpack1('m0') is strict Base64: it raises ArgumentError on invalid
        # input, matching Base64.strict_decode64 without requiring the
        # base64 gem (no longer a default gem as of Ruby 3.5).
        bytes = vector.unpack1('m0')

        case (output_dtype || 'float').to_s
        when 'float' then bytes.unpack('e*')
        when 'int8', 'binary' then bytes.unpack('c*')
        when 'uint8', 'ubinary' then bytes.unpack('C*')
        else raise ArgumentError, "Unsupported Voyage output dtype: #{output_dtype.inspect}"
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RubyLLM
  module Voyage
    # One document returned by a reranking request.
    RerankResult = Struct.new(:index, :relevance_score, :document, keyword_init: true)

    # Typed result returned by {Voyage.rerank}.
    Reranking = Struct.new(:results, :model, :input_tokens, keyword_init: true) do
      # Reorders the original candidate collection by relevance.
      #
      # Pass the same collection whose contents were sent as +documents:+.
      # Returns the matching items in reranked order, truncated to +top_k+
      # when one was requested.
      #
      # @param collection [Array, #to_a] candidates in their original order
      # @return [Array] the reranked items
      # @raise [IndexError] when the collection is smaller than the
      #   document list that was reranked
      #
      # @example
      #   reranking = RubyLLM::Voyage.rerank(
      #     query: query, documents: articles.map(&:content), top_k: 5
      #   )
      #   reranking.reorder(articles) # => the five most relevant articles
      def reorder(collection)
        items = collection.to_a
        results.map { |result| items.fetch(result.index) }
      end
    end

    # One contextualized chunk and its vector.
    ContextualizedChunk = Struct.new(:embedding, :index, :text, keyword_init: true) do
      # Summarizes the vector so console output stays readable.
      # @return [String]
      def inspect
        dimensions = embedding.respond_to?(:length) ? "[#{embedding.length} values]" : embedding.inspect
        "#<RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedChunk index=#{index} embedding=#{dimensions} " \
          "text=#{text&.slice(0, 60).inspect}>"
      end
    end

    # Contextualized chunks belonging to one input document or query.
    ContextualizedResult = Struct.new(:chunks, :index, keyword_init: true)

    # Typed result returned by {Voyage.contextualized_embed}.
    ContextualizedEmbedding = Struct.new(
      :results,
      :model,
      :input_tokens,
      :chunker_version,
      keyword_init: true
    )

    # Metadata for a file managed by Voyage's Files API.
    VoyageFile = Struct.new(
      :id,
      :object,
      :purpose,
      :filename,
      :bytes,
      :created_at,
      :expires_at,
      :raw,
      keyword_init: true
    )

    # A cursor-based page returned by a Voyage list endpoint.
    Page = Struct.new(:data, :first_id, :last_id, :has_more, :raw, keyword_init: true)

    # Result of an all-or-nothing bulk file deletion.
    FileDeletion = Struct.new(:file_ids, :deleted, :raw, keyword_init: true)
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RubyLLM
  # Provider implementations registered with RubyLLM.
  module Providers
    # Voyage retrieval API provider for RubyLLM.
    #
    # Most applications should use +RubyLLM.embed+ or
    # {RubyLLM::Voyage.embed} instead of instantiating this class directly.
    class Voyage < Provider
      require 'ruby_llm/providers/voyage/embeddings'
      require 'ruby_llm/providers/voyage/reranking'
      require 'ruby_llm/providers/voyage/contextualized_embeddings'
      require 'ruby_llm/providers/voyage/files'

      include Voyage::Embeddings
      include Voyage::Reranking
      include Voyage::ContextualizedEmbeddings
      include Voyage::Files

      # Returns the configured Voyage API base URL.
      # @return [String]
      def api_base
        @config.voyage_api_base || 'https://api.voyageai.com/v1'
      end

      # Returns authentication headers for Voyage requests.
      # @return [Hash{String => String}]
      def headers
        { 'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@config.voyage_api_key}" }
      end

      # RubyLLM 1.x does not expose per-request provider options for embeddings,
      # so the extension's facade calls this richer provider method directly.
      #
      # @api private
      # @param text [String, Array<String>]
      # @param model [String]
      # @param dimensions [Integer, nil]
      # @param provider_options [Hash]
      # @return [RubyLLM::Embedding]
      def embed(text, model:, dimensions: nil, provider_options: {}, **options)
        payload = render_embedding_payload(text, model:, dimensions:, **options)
                  .merge(provider_options.transform_keys(&:to_sym))
        response = @connection.post(embedding_url(model:), payload)
        parse_embedding_response(response, model:, text:, output_dtype: payload[:output_dtype])
      end

      class << self
        # Lists configuration keys registered for the Voyage provider.
        # @return [Array<Symbol>]
        # @api private
        def configuration_options
          %i[
            voyage_api_key
            voyage_api_base
            voyage_default_input_type
            voyage_default_truncation
            voyage_default_output_dimension
            voyage_default_output_dtype
            voyage_default_encoding_format
          ]
        end

        # Lists configuration keys required to use the Voyage provider.
        # @return [Array<Symbol>]
        # @api private
        def configuration_requirements
          %i[voyage_api_key]
        end

        # Indicates that Voyage model IDs can be used without registry entries.
        # @return [Boolean]
        def assume_models_exist?
          true
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RubyLLM
  # Voyage retrieval integration for RubyLLM.
  #
  # Use {.embed_query} and {.embed_documents} for the two sides of retrieval,
  # {.embed} for request-level Voyage options, or the conventional
  # +RubyLLM.embed(..., provider: :voyage)+ interface.
  module Voyage
    # Current gem version.
    VERSION = '0.1.0'

    # Internal sentinel used to distinguish an omitted option from an explicit
    # +nil+ value.
    # @api private
    UNSET = Object.new.freeze
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RubyLLM
  module Providers
    class Voyage
      # Voyage contextualized chunk embedding mapping.
      # @api private
      module ContextualizedEmbeddings
        # Executes a contextualized chunk embedding request.
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedEmbedding]
        def contextualized_embed(inputs, model:, input_type: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET, dimensions: nil,
                                 output_dtype: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET,
                                 encoding_format: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET, auto_chunk: nil, chunk_size: nil,
                                 chunk_overlap: nil, provider_options: {})
          payload = {
            inputs: inputs,
            model: model,
            input_type: contextualized_option(input_type, :voyage_default_input_type),
            output_dimension: dimensions || @config.voyage_default_output_dimension,
            output_dtype: contextualized_option(output_dtype, :voyage_default_output_dtype),
            encoding_format: contextualized_option(encoding_format, :voyage_default_encoding_format),
            enable_auto_chunking: auto_chunk,
            chunk_size: chunk_size,
            chunk_overlap: chunk_overlap
          }.compact.merge(provider_options.transform_keys(&:to_sym))
          response = @connection.post('contextualizedembeddings', payload)
          parse_contextualized_response(response, output_dtype: payload[:output_dtype])
        end

        private

        def contextualized_option(value, config_key)
          value = @config.public_send(config_key) if value.equal?(RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET)
          value&.to_s
        end

        def parse_contextualized_response(response, output_dtype: nil)
          body = response.body
          results = body.fetch('data').map do |group|
            chunks = group.fetch('data').map do |item|
              vector = item.fetch('embedding')
              vector = RubyLLM::Voyage::VectorDecoder.decode(vector, output_dtype) if vector.is_a?(String)
              RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedChunk.new(
                embedding: vector,
                index: item.fetch('index'),
                text: item['text']
              )
            end
            RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedResult.new(chunks: chunks, index: group.fetch('index'))
          end

          RubyLLM::Voyage::ContextualizedEmbedding.new(
            results: results,
            model: body['model'],
            input_tokens: body.dig('usage', 'total_tokens') || 0,
            chunker_version: body['chunker_version']
          )
        end

      # Voyage embeddings request and response mapping.
      # @api private
      module Embeddings
        # Returns the embeddings endpoint relative to the configured API base.
        # @return [String]
        # @api private
        def embedding_url(...)
          'embeddings'
        end

        # Converts RubyLLM embedding arguments to a Voyage request body.
        # A +nil+ dimensions argument falls back to the configured
        # +voyage_default_output_dimension+.
        # @param text [String, Array<String>]
        # @param model [String]
        # @param dimensions [Integer, nil]
        # @param input_type [String, Symbol, nil]
        # @param truncation [Boolean, nil]
        # @param output_dtype [String, Symbol, nil]
        # @param encoding_format [String, Symbol, nil]
        # @return [Hash]
        # @api private
        def render_embedding_payload(text, model:, dimensions: nil, input_type: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET,
                                     truncation: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET, output_dtype: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET,
                                     encoding_format: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET)
          {
            model: model,
            input: text,
            input_type: enum_option(input_type, :voyage_default_input_type),
            truncation: configured_option(truncation, :voyage_default_truncation),
            output_dimension: dimensions || @config.voyage_default_output_dimension,
            output_dtype: enum_option(output_dtype, :voyage_default_output_dtype),
            encoding_format: enum_option(encoding_format, :voyage_default_encoding_format)
          }.compact
        end

        # Converts a Voyage response into a RubyLLM embedding result.
        # @param response [Faraday::Response]
        # @param model [String]
        # @param text [String, Array<String>]
        # @param output_dtype [String, Symbol, nil]
        # @return [RubyLLM::Embedding]
        # @raise [KeyError] when the response omits embedding data
        # @raise [ArgumentError] when Base64 data or its output type is invalid
        # @api private
        def parse_embedding_response(response, model:, text:, output_dtype: nil)
          data = response.body
          vectors = data.fetch('data').map { |item| item.fetch('embedding') }
          if vectors.first.is_a?(String)
            vectors.map! do |vector|
              RubyLLM::Voyage::VectorDecoder.decode(vector, output_dtype)
            end
          end
          vectors = vectors.first if vectors.length == 1 && !text.is_a?(Array)

          Embedding.new(
            vectors: vectors,
            model: data['model'] || model,
            input_tokens: data.dig('usage', 'total_tokens') || 0
          )
        end

        private

        def configured_option(value, config_key)
          value.equal?(RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET) ? @config.public_send(config_key) : value
        end

        def enum_option(value, config_key)
          configured_option(value, config_key)&.to_s
        end
      end
    end
  end

module RubyLLM
  module Providers
    class Voyage
      # Voyage reranking request and response mapping.
      # @api private
      module Reranking
        # Executes a Voyage reranking request.
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::Reranking]
        def rerank(query:, documents:, model:, top_k: nil, return_documents: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET,
                   truncation: RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET, provider_options: {})
          payload = {
            query: query,
            documents: documents,
            model: model,
            top_k: top_k,
            return_documents: return_documents,
            truncation: truncation
          }.reject { |_key, value| value.nil? || value.equal?(RubyLLM::Voyage::UNSET) }
           .merge(provider_options.transform_keys(&:to_sym))
          response = @connection.post('rerank', payload)
          parse_rerank_response(response)
        end

        private

        def parse_rerank_response(response)
          body = response.body
          results = body.fetch('data').map do |item|
            RubyLLM::Voyage::RerankResult.new(
              index: item.fetch('index'),
              relevance_score: item.fetch('relevance_score'),
              document: item['document']
            )
          end

          RubyLLM::Voyage::Reranking.new(
            results: results,
            model: body['model'],
            input_tokens: body.dig('usage', 'total_tokens') || 0
          )
        end
      end
    end
  end

require 'uri'

module RubyLLM
  module Providers
    class Voyage
      # Voyage Files API operations.
      # @api private
      module Files
        # Maximum redirect hops followed when downloading file content.
        MAX_DOWNLOAD_REDIRECTS = 3
        private_constant :MAX_DOWNLOAD_REDIRECTS

        # Uploads one JSONL file.
        # @param path [String, Pathname]
        # @param purpose [String]
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::VoyageFile]
        def upload_file(path, purpose: 'batch')
          expanded = File.expand_path(path)
          unless File.extname(expanded).casecmp?('.jsonl')
            raise ArgumentError, 'Voyage file uploads must use the .jsonl extension'
          end

          # RubyLLM's connection stack loads faraday-multipart and uses this
          # same class for its own uploads; 1.x has no public helper for it.
          part = Faraday::Multipart::FilePart.new(expanded, 'application/jsonl', File.basename(expanded))
          response = @connection.post('files', { file: part, purpose: purpose })
          parse_file(response.body)
        end

        # Retrieves file metadata.
        # @param file_id [String]
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::VoyageFile]
        def retrieve_file(file_id)
          parse_file(@connection.get("files/#{escape_id(file_id)}").body)
        end

        # Lists file metadata with cursor pagination.
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::Page]
        def list_files(purpose: nil, limit: nil, order: nil, after: nil)
          query = URI.encode_www_form({ purpose: purpose, limit: limit, order: order, after: after }.compact)
          path = query.empty? ? 'files' : "files?#{query}"
          parse_page(@connection.get(path).body) { |item| parse_file(item) }
        end

        # Downloads raw file content.
        # @param file_id [String]
        # @return [String]
        def file_content(file_id)
          response = @connection.get("files/#{escape_id(file_id)}/content") do |request|
            request.headers['Accept'] = 'text/plain'
          end
          return response.body unless response.status.between?(300, 399)

          download_redirect(response.headers['location'])
        end

        # Atomically deletes one or more files. Voyage treats the operation
        # as all-or-nothing and reports the outcome in a +success+ field,
        # with +error_file_ids+ available in +raw+ on failure.
        # @param file_ids [Array<String>]
        # @return [RubyLLM::Voyage::FileDeletion]
        def delete_files(file_ids)
          body = @connection.post('files/delete', { file_ids: file_ids }).body
          deleted = body.is_a?(Hash) && body.key?('success') ? body['success'] : true
          RubyLLM::Voyage::FileDeletion.new(file_ids: file_ids, deleted: deleted, raw: body)
        end

        private

        def parse_file(item)
          RubyLLM::Voyage::VoyageFile.new(
            id: item['id'], object: item['object'], purpose: item['purpose'], filename: item['filename'],
            bytes: item['bytes'], created_at: item['created_at'], expires_at: item['expires_at'], raw: item
          )
        end

        def parse_page(body, &)
          RubyLLM::Voyage::Page.new(
            data: body.fetch('data').map(&),
            first_id: body['first_id'], last_id: body['last_id'], has_more: body['has_more'], raw: body
          )
        end

        def escape_id(id)
          URI.encode_www_form_component(id.to_s)
        end

        def download_redirect(location)
          connection = download_connection

          MAX_DOWNLOAD_REDIRECTS.times do
            uri = validated_redirect_uri(location)
            response = connection.get(uri.to_s) { |request| request.headers['Accept'] = 'text/plain' }
            return response.body unless response.status.between?(300, 399)

            location = response.headers['location']
          end

          raise RubyLLM::Error, 'Voyage file download followed too many redirects'
        end

        def validated_redirect_uri(location)
          uri = URI(location.to_s)
          unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTPS) && uri.host && !uri.userinfo
            raise RubyLLM::Error, 'Voyage returned an unsafe file download redirect'
          end

          uri
        end

        # Signed storage URLs must be fetched outside the provider connection
        # so the Voyage Authorization header is not forwarded. Uses RubyLLM's
        # own side-connection builder and honors its configured adapter and
        # timeout.
        def download_connection
          RubyLLM::Connection.basic do |faraday|
            faraday.options.timeout = @config.request_timeout
            faraday.adapter(@config.faraday_adapter || :net_http)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# ruby_llm-voyage

[![CI](https://github.com/dinsley/ruby_llm-voyage/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dinsley/ruby_llm-voyage/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Gem Version](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ruby_llm-voyage.svg)](https://rubygems.org/gems/ruby_llm-voyage)

[Voyage AI](https://docs.voyageai.com/) builds embedding and reranking models
for search and retrieval. This gem adds them to
[RubyLLM](https://rubyllm.com/): document and query embeddings, reranking,
contextualized chunk embeddings, and the Files API.

Requires Ruby 3.1.3+ and RubyLLM 1.16+.

## Installation

Add the gem to your Gemfile:

```ruby
gem 'ruby_llm-voyage'
```

Then configure your API key (created in the [Voyage dashboard](https://dashboard.voyageai.com/)):

```ruby
RubyLLM.configure do |config|
  config.voyage_api_key = ENV.fetch('VOYAGE_API_KEY')
end
```

## Your first embedding

Voyage works through the standard RubyLLM embedding interface:

```ruby
embedding = RubyLLM.embed(
  'Ruby is optimized for programmer happiness.',
  model: 'voyage-4',
  provider: :voyage
)

embedding.vectors      # => [0.018, -0.032, ...]
embedding.input_tokens # => 9
```

Pass an array to embed a batch in one request, and `dimensions:` to control vector size:

```ruby
RubyLLM.embed(%w[Ruby Rails], model: 'voyage-4-lite', provider: :voyage, dimensions: 512)
```

Voyage tunes vectors differently for the text you store (`document`) and the text people search with (`query`), and using
both sides improves retrieval quality. The gem gives each side its own method:

```ruby
RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_documents(['Reset your password from account settings.'])
RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_query('how do I reset my password')
```

Both return the same `RubyLLM::Embedding` object and use `config.default_embedding_model` when `model:` is omitted.

For the remaining options — truncation, quantized output, an explicit `nil` input type — use `RubyLLM::Voyage.embed`:

```ruby
embedding = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed(
  'How do I reset my password?',
  model: 'voyage-4-lite',
  input_type: 'query',
  truncation: false,
  dimensions: 512
)
```

## Semantic search in Rails

Here's a complete search feature for a help center, using [Neighbor](https://github.com/ankane/neighbor) and PostgreSQL's pgvector
extension.

Set up the gems and configure the embedding defaults once:

```ruby
# Gemfile
gem 'ruby_llm-voyage'
gem 'neighbor'
```

```ruby
# config/initializers/ruby_llm.rb
RubyLLM.configure do |config|
  config.voyage_api_key = [REDACTED]
  config.default_embedding_model = 'voyage-4-lite'
  config.voyage_default_output_dimension = 512
end
```

Then the vector column:

```sh
bin/rails generate neighbor:vector
bin/rails db:migrate
```

```ruby
class AddEmbeddingToArticles < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.0]
  def change
    add_column :articles, :embedding, :vector, limit: 512

    add_column :articles, :embedding_model, :string   # Identifies rows that need re-embedding when you upgrade models
    add_column :articles, :embedding_digest, :string  # Digest of the embedded data to track changes to the field
    add_column :articles, :embedded_at, :datetime     # Identifies when the data last had its embedding created

    add_index :articles, :embedding, using: :hnsw, opclass: :vector_cosine_ops
    add_index :articles, :embedding_model
  end
end
```

Embed in the background as articles are created or updated:

```ruby
class Article < ApplicationRecord
  has_neighbors :embedding

  after_save_commit -> { EmbedArticleJob.perform_later(self) }, if: :saved_change_to_content?

  def refresh_embedding!
    digest = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(content)
    return if embedding_digest == digest

    result = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_documents(content)

    update_columns(
      embedding: result.vectors,
      embedding_model: result.model,
      embedding_digest: digest,
      embedded_at: Time.zone.current
    )
  end
end

class EmbedArticleJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(article) = article.refresh_embedding!
end
```

Then search with a query embedding:

```ruby
class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def search
    query_vector = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_query(params[:q]).vectors

    @articles = Article.nearest_neighbors(
      :embedding, query_vector, distance: 'cosine'
    ).first(10)
  end
end
```

### Embedding an entire table

The per-record job above handles ongoing writes, but backfilling existing data one row at a time wastes
API calls. Embed whole tables in batches instead — each batch is one request, and Voyage accepts up to
1,000 texts per request ([current limits](https://docs.voyageai.com/reference/embeddings-api)):

```ruby
class Article < ApplicationRecord
  def self.embed_missing!(batch_size: 100)
    where(embedding: nil).find_in_batches(batch_size: batch_size) do |batch|
      result = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_documents(batch.map(&:content))

      batch.zip(result.vectors) do |(article, vector)|
        article.update_columns(
          embedding: vector,
          embedding_model: result.model,
          embedding_digest: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(article.content),
          embedded_at: Time.current
        )
      end
    end
  end
end

Article.embed_missing!
```

The provenance columns make model upgrades a repeat of the same procedure:
clear the vectors built with the old model, backfill, and switch the query
side once nothing is left to embed.

```ruby
Article.where.not(embedding_model: 'voyage-4').update_all(embedding: nil)
Article.embed_missing!
```

## Better results with reranking

Vector search is fast but approximate. When result order matters, fetch a generous candidate
set with vector search, then let a [Voyage reranker](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/reranker) put
the best matches first:

```ruby
question = 'How do I configure SAML SSO?'
query_vector = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_query(question).vectors

candidates = Article.nearest_neighbors(
  :embedding, query_vector, distance: 'cosine'
).first(25)

reranking = RubyLLM::Voyage.rerank(
  query: question,
  documents: candidates.map(&:content),
  model: 'rerank-2.5-lite',
  top_k: 5
)

best_articles = reranking.reorder(candidates) # the 5 most relevant records
```

`reorder` maps the reranked positions back onto the collection you passed as
`documents:`. Each result also carries the original `index`, a
`relevance_score`, and (with `return_documents: true`) the document text.

Rerankers score every candidate against the query, so rerank a small candidate set rather than the whole corpus.

## Embedding long documents with context

Chunking a long document strips each chunk of its surroundings: a handbook chunk that reads "this does not apply during the probation period" no longer
says which policy it belongs to. Voyage's [contextualized models](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/contextualized-chunk-embeddings) embed each chunk with
information from the rest of its document.

Pass pre-chunked documents as nested arrays:

```ruby
result = RubyLLM::Voyage.contextualized_embed(
  [
    ['Vacation policy overview', 'Accrual rates by tenure', 'Carryover rules'],
    ['Remote work policy', 'Equipment stipend', 'Home office requirements']
  ],
  model: 'voyage-context-4',
  input_type: :document,
  dimensions: 512
)

result.results.each do |document|
  document.chunks.each do |chunk|
    # document.index, chunk.index, chunk.embedding
  end
end
```

Or let Voyage do the chunking server-side:

```ruby
result = RubyLLM::Voyage.contextualized_embed(
  [handbook.full_text],
  model: 'voyage-context-4',
  input_type: :document,
  dimensions: 512,
  auto_chunk: true,
  chunk_size: 512,
  chunk_overlap: 0
)

result.results.first.chunks.each do |chunk|
  HandbookChunk.create!(
    position: chunk.index,
    content: chunk.text,   # the exact text this vector represents
    embedding: chunk.embedding
  )
end
```

With `auto_chunk`, store `chunk.text` alongside each vector, and query the
index with the same contextualized model.

## Giving a chatbot search

A RubyLLM tool can embed the model's search query with Voyage and pull
matching articles out of your database:

```ruby
class SearchKnowledgeBase < RubyLLM::Tool
  desc 'Search the help center for articles relevant to a question'

  param :query, desc: 'A concise search query'

  def execute(query:)
    query_vector = RubyLLM::Voyage.embed_query(query).vectors

    Article.nearest_neighbors(:embedding, query_vector, distance: 'cosine')
           .first(5)
           .map { |article| { id: article.id, content: article.content } }
           .to_json
  end
end

chat = RubyLLM.chat(model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5')
chat.with_instructions('Answer using the knowledge base. Cite article IDs.')
chat.with_tool(SearchKnowledgeBase)

chat.ask('How do I set up single sign-on?')
```

If articles are scoped per account, filter the `nearest_neighbors` query by the current user's permissions before returning results to the model.

## Batch workflows with the Files API

Voyage's asynchronous [batch workflows](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/batch-inference) exchange JSONL files. This gem covers the full file lifecycle:

```ruby
uploaded = RubyLLM::Voyage.upload_file('requests.jsonl')

RubyLLM::Voyage.retrieve_file(uploaded.id)   # metadata
RubyLLM::Voyage.list_files(purpose: 'batch') # cursor-paginated listing
RubyLLM::Voyage.file_content(uploaded.id)    # raw JSONL back out

RubyLLM::Voyage.delete_files([uploaded.id])
```

`find_file` and `download_file` are aliases of `retrieve_file` and `file_content`, matching RubyLLM's own file-method naming.

Downloads follow Voyage's redirect to a signed storage URL without forwarding your API key, and refuse non-HTTPS redirects.

## Configuration reference

Every Voyage option can be set globally, per `RubyLLM.context`, or per
request:

```ruby
RubyLLM.configure do |config|
  config.voyage_api_key = ENV.fetch('VOYAGE_API_KEY')
  config.default_embedding_model = 'voyage-4-lite'  # when model: is omitted
  config.voyage_default_output_dimension = 512      # when dimensions: is omitted
  config.voyage_default_input_type = 'document'
  config.voyage_default_truncation = false          # error instead of truncating
  config.voyage_default_output_dtype = 'float'
  config.voyage_default_encoding_format = 'base64'
  config.voyage_api_base = 'https://api.voyageai.com/v1'
end
```

Request-level options on `RubyLLM::Voyage.embed` (and on `embed_query` /
`embed_documents`, which fix `input_type` for you):

| Option | Voyage field | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model:` | `model` | Any Voyage embedding model ID |
| `input_type:` | `input_type` | `query`, `document`, or `nil` |
| `truncation:` | `truncation` | `true` or `false` |
| `dimensions:` | `output_dimension` | Model-dependent |
| `output_dtype:` | `output_dtype` | `float`, `int8`, `uint8`, `binary`, `ubinary` |
| `encoding_format:` | `encoding_format` | `base64` or `nil` |
| `provider_options:` | merged into request | Fields the gem doesn't have a keyword for yet |

## Not supported

- **Multimodal embeddings** (`voyage-multimodal-3.5`) — text inputs only.
- **Batch jobs** — the Files API is covered, but creating and managing
  asynchronous batch jobs is not.
- **Token counting** — Voyage's official SDKs tokenize locally; this gem
  reports `input_tokens` from API responses instead.
- **Request splitting** — one call sends one API request. Collections over
  Voyage's 1,000-text limit must be batched by the caller, as in the
  backfill example above.

New Voyage request fields usually work before the gem names them: pass them through `provider_options:`. For anything else, open an [issue](https://github.com/dinsley/ruby_llm-voyage/issues).

  def test_optional_live_file_lifecycle

    exercise_live_file_lifecycle
  end

  private

  # Kept out of the test method so its ensure-based cleanup only runs when
  # the VOYAGE_LIVE_FILES gate is open, never on a skipped test.
  def exercise_live_file_lifecycle
    uploaded = nil
    Tempfile.create(['voyage-live', '.jsonl']) do |file|
      file.write(%({"custom_id":"live-one","body":{"input":"Ruby"}}\n))
      file.flush
      uploaded = RubyLLM::Voyage.upload_file(file.path)

      assert_equal uploaded.id, RubyLLM::Voyage.retrieve_file(uploaded.id).id
      assert_includes RubyLLM::Voyage.list_files(purpose: 'batch').data.map(&:id), uploaded.id
      WebMock.allow_net_connect!
      begin
        assert_includes RubyLLM::Voyage.file_content(uploaded.id), 'live-one'
      ensure
        WebMock.disable_net_connect!(allow: 'api.voyageai.com')
      end
    end
  ensure
    RubyLLM::Voyage.delete_files([uploaded.id]) if uploaded&.id
  end

  def live_embed(text, dimensions: 256, **options)
    RubyLLM::Voyage.embed(
      text,
      model: MODEL,
      dimensions: dimensions,
      truncation: false,
      **options
    )
  end

  def embedding_context(input_type)
    RubyLLM.context do |config|
      config.voyage_default_input_type = input_type
    end
  end

  def cosine_similarity(left, right)
    dot_product = left.zip(right).sum { |a, b| a * b }
    left_norm = Math.sqrt(left.sum { |value| value * value })
    right_norm = Math.sqrt(right.sum { |value| value * value })
    dot_product / (left_norm * right_norm)
  end

  def assert_embedding(result)
    assert_instance_of RubyLLM::Embedding, result
    assert_equal MODEL, result.model
    assert_operator result.input_tokens, :>, 0
  end

  def assert_vector(vector, dtype:, dimensions:)
    expected_length = %w[binary ubinary].include?(dtype) ? dimensions / 8 : dimensions

    assert_equal expected_length, vector.length

    case dtype
    when 'float' then assert(vector.all?(Float))
    when 'int8', 'binary' then assert_integer_range(vector, -128..127)
    when 'uint8', 'ubinary' then assert_integer_range(vector, 0..255)
    end
  end

  def assert_integer_range(vector, range)
    assert vector.all?(Integer)
    assert(vector.all? { |value| range.cover?(value) })
  end
end
